Every Hindu temple is built in principle on the Vāstupuruṣamaṇḍala, a ritual diagram that regulates but is not the ground-plan.
Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra ch. LIX gives the Vāstu measure of the building containing the sanctuary, with 6 squares for the Prāsāda.
The Vāstupuruṣamaṇḍala is in principle square, divided into compartments with diagonals; knowledge of it forms the first part of the science of architecture (Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra ch. XLV).
